facts.statement: The genus Dipterus was established by Adam Sedgwick and Roderick Murchison in 1828.
Dipterus was an extinct genus of freshwater lungfish that lived during the middle Devonian period in Europe and possibly North America.
facts.quote: Dipterus (from , 'two' and 'wing') is an extinct genus of freshwater lungfish from the middle Devonian period of Europe and potentially North America.

facts.statement: Dipterus was about 35 cm long and closely resembled modern lungfish in most respects.
facts.quote: In most respects, Dipterus, which was about 35 cm long, closely resembled modern lungfish.

facts.statement: Unlike modern lungfish where the dorsal, caudal, and anal fins are fused, Dipterus had separate fins.
facts.quote: However, unlike its modern relatives, in which the dorsal, caudal, and anal fin are fused into one, Dipterus's fins were still separated.

facts.statement: Dipterus measured about 35 cm (14 inches) in length and closely resembled modern lungfish in most aspects.
facts.quote: En la mayoría de los aspectos, Dipterus, que medía unos 35 cm (14 pulgadas) de longitud, se parecía mucho a los peces pulmonados modernos.

facts.statement: Dipterus is classified within the class Dipnoi.
Dipterus belongs to the family Dipteridae.
Dipterus lived from the Eifelian to the Famennian stages, between 393.47 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Famennian (393.47 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dipterus was one of the first lungfish to be described by science.
facts.quote: Fue uno de los primeros peces pulmonados descritos científicamente.

facts.statement: It is debated whether many other species described from isolated tooth plates from Europe and North America truly belong to Dipterus due to their fragmentary nature.
facts.quote: Many other species from Europe and North America have also been described based on isolated tooth plates, though due to their fragmentary nature, their exact taxonomic affinity is uncertain.

rejected.statement: Dipterus possessed tooth-like plates on its palate instead of real teeth, similar to its ancestor Dipnorhynchus.
rejected.quote: Like its ancestor Dipnorhynchus, it had tooth-like plates on its palate instead of real teeth.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'tooth-like plates on its palate instead of real'

rejected.quote: El género fue establecido por Adam Sedgwick y Roderick Murchison en 1828.
